key_insight: TongGeometry uses a guided tree-search loop that both proposes and solves olympiad‑level geometry problems, discovering problems that are simultaneously hard and elegantly concise.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between automatic problem generation and high-level mathematical reasoning by producing and verifying challenging olympiad geometry problems that humans find meaningful and nontrivial.
method: Guided tree search that explores construction and proof trees to generate candidate geometry problems and attempt their solutions.
A scoring/heuristic mechanism that prioritizes problems balancing difficulty and conciseness, driving search toward elegant, hard instances.
A closed-loop propose-and-solve pipeline: generation proposes problems, the solver attempts proofs, feedback refines future search.
impact: Enables automated discovery of high-quality mathematical problems and advances scalable symbolic/structured reasoning techniques; useful for benchmarks, curriculum generation, and improving models that handle complex structured reasoning.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the propose-and-solve loop (generation → solver → feedback → refined generation).
Example geometry problem with annotated construction and a highlighted concise proof tree.
Chart showing trade-off between problem difficulty and conciseness with discovered examples along the frontier.
Icon set: tree-search, magnifying glass (difficulty), pencil/proof (solution verification).
paper_title: Proposing and solving olympiad geometry with guided tree search
paper_authors: Chi Zhang, Jiajun Song, Siyu Li, Yitao Liang, Yuxi Ma
